items.source: Issue #152 worker discovery, joint Application Client and Local Daemon adjudication, and operator decision

evidence.details: The public client delegated attach and bounded repair to connect-or-spawn, which derived both the spawn command and expected server image from the consumer executable. External Watcher and Station binaries therefore could not start or authenticate the shared Telex daemon through only the supported client.

items.description: Provide production installed-current daemon selection from an explicitly trusted root, with one immutable manifest-validated target shared by spawn and pre-Hello authentication under Local Daemon selector admission.
items.affectedOutcome: Issue #152 must prove executable public consumer runtime behavior; compile-only fixtures cannot establish consumer consumability.
items.requiredness: Required in the current client-conformance PR.
items.sequencing: Direct-main task and both current-design authorities land before the frozen issue #152 worker resumes. Product implementation, design promotion, review, CI, cross-platform and cross-backend proof, consumer attestations, and design inspection then remain in the same PR.
items.disposition: Absorb the Application Client public bootstrap policy, typed failures, runtime fixtures, and product-design promotion in client-conformance; consume Local Daemon trust item application-client-daemon-bootstrap-trust-v1 without duplicating its lock, token, admission, or readiness-publication ownership.
items.owner: Application Client workstream orchestrator with Local Daemon trust authority
items.terminalPath: Complete InstalledCurrent implementation and product-design promotion in issue #152, prove the exact head on Windows and Linux against SQLite and credentialed Postgres with public Watcher and Station fixtures, then pass final implementation review, required CI, consumer attestations, and exact-head design inspection.

Local Daemon item application-client-daemon-bootstrap-trust-v1 is not changed here and remains with its owner.

items.source: Issue #152 source integration after the published v0.2.1 baseline, campaign verification, and operator decision

evidence.details: Published v0.2.1 has root package version 0.2.1 and an exhaustive public ApplicationClientError, and its docs/application-client-core.md says no published release contains the binding. The accepted issue #152 surface adds ApplicationClientError::DaemonBootstrap(DaemonBootstrapFailure) and marks the enum non-exhaustive, which breaks Rust source compatibility against that published baseline.
exclusions: No tag creation or movement, Release workflow dispatch, or GitHub, crates.io, or plugin publication.
No change to published v0.2.1 or held v0.2.0 source, assets, or history.
No daemon protocol or schema version change from package versioning.
No installed-fleet, shared-store, operator daemon, or persistent PATH action, and no automatic gate, hardening, or campaign closure.

items.description: Move the root package to unpublished source version 0.3.0 in the issue #152 PR, with genuinely coupled metadata and source-consumer migration guidance, instead of shipping a breaking source change under 0.2.x.
items.affectedOutcome: The conformance bundle's public Rust surface follows the root-crate source compatibility policy against the released v0.2.1 baseline.
items.requiredness: Required in the current client-conformance PR.
items.sequencing: Parallel with implementation in the same PR; no new node, worker, acknowledgement, or artifact-before-code hold. Exact-head review, CI, design inspection, and campaign merge authorization still apply.
items.disposition: Absorb in client-conformance. Change the root Cargo.toml version and its Cargo.lock entry to 0.3.0. Update every plugin, marketplace, bootstrap, proof-default, and version-fixture surface that existing lockstep tests couple to it. Correct public documentation to name v0.2.1 as the released baseline and 0.3.0 as unpublished source. Document migration for typed bootstrap errors and non-exhaustive matching. Independent versions and historical fixtures stay unchanged unless genuinely coupled; decoupling or weakening tests needs a separate policy decision.
items.terminalPath: The issue #152 PR merges with the coupled 0.3.0 source version and migration documentation after exact-head review, required CI, consumer attestations, design inspection, and campaign authorization. Any later tag or publication requires a separate operator decision.

completionEvidence.details: PR #161 merged the coupled unpublished 0.3.0 source version and migration documentation after exact-head review, required CI, consumer attestations, and design inspection, under App's normal guarded merge authorization. Under the 2026-10-22 user correction, the implementer, supported by App, owns the merge flow, and the campaign's added merge-floor certification was withdrawn. No tag or publication occurred; any later tag or publication still requires a separate operator decision.
